about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2018 only.

rows.detail: This chart is the ONLY per-town Monty Tech enrollment figure in the FY2018 report, because the four tables that carried per-town data in FY2017 (foundation enrollment comparison, assessment ratios, community assessments, twenty-year assessment history) are all absent this year.

rows.table: District and school accountability classification, 2018
rows.detail: This table has NO FY2017 counterpart because the accountability system changed: FY2017 reported Levels 1-5, which DESE discontinued, so the two years cannot be compared on this measure.

rows.table: FY2019 omnibus budget by line number
rows.detail: Line numbering is continuous with FY2017's, which is what makes mid-year amendment votes readable.

rows.table: Paid vacation schedule by years of service
rows.detail: The first row is corrupted in extraction: '10 Months Less than one complete year of continuous service | 808 hours per each full calendar month up to 80 hours' -- the '808' is a collision of the struck-through '8' and the replacement '8 hours per month', because the whole article is printed with additions underlined and deletions struck through and the strike-through markup does not survive extraction.

rows.table: Departmental budget changes for FY2019
rows.detail: FY2017's equivalent report was continuous prose with only a handful of figures; this year's is itemised, so the two years are not comparable in structure.

Article 7 of the November Special Town Meeting reprints an entire bylaw section with additions underlined and deletions struck through, but the strike-through markup does not survive text extraction, so the extracted text runs the old and new wording together ('payable on the last first payroll warrant in Julyne') and the paid-vacation table's first row collides into a nonexistent '808 hours'.

rows.table: Police activity statistics, 2018
rows.detail: THREE THINGS TO WATCH: (1) the report gives the calls-for-service increase as '13.7%' in one sentence and '13.6%' two paragraphs later; (2) the sentence 'In the first half of fiscal 2017, staff assignments had to be increased 75 times' is copied verbatim from the FY2017 report and still says 2017 -- it is stale text, not a 2018 figure; (3) the K-9 deployment count of 27 is also identical to FY2017's.

rows.table: Monty Tech member towns
rows.detail: Identical to FY2017 p123.

rows.table: Monty Tech AP exam results, six-year review
rows.detail: The five overlapping year columns are identical to FY2017's printing, so the series is consistent.

rows.table: Valuation and tax history, five years
rows.detail: Small, but they mean the two reports are not byte-identical on shared years.

The entire Monty Tech FINANCIAL section is missing. FY2017 carried eight Monty Tech tables at pp140-149 -- balance sheet, budget summary, five-year income and expense, expenditures by DESE function code, DESE's Chapter 70 worksheet, foundation enrollment vs school attending children, assessment ratio percentages, community assessments, and a twenty-year assessment history. FY2018's Monty Tech section stops at p149 with the school committee roster and contains NONE of them. Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment appears in FY2018 only as a single omnibus budget line. A search for 'COMMUNITY ASSESSMENTS' or 'ASSESSMENT HISTORY' returns nothing in this document.

The FY2018 report silently corrects a digit-drop in the FY2017 report. FY2017 printed 2017 Bond Anticipation Notes as $295,925 and total outstanding indebtedness as $52,093,784; FY2018's five-year debt table prints the same year as $2,895,925 and $54,693,785 -- and FY2017's own balance sheet said BANS PAYABLE $2,895,925.00. Neither report flags the correction.

The FY2019 omnibus budget table foots to $36,804,408.83 under a heading and an article vote that both say $36,867,903.83, and the Town Manager's report gives a third figure, $36,813,954.63, for the same budget. All three are in this one document.

Monty Tech's per-program gender split vanished. FY2017 gave male/female counts for all twenty vocational programs in parentheticals; FY2018 gives only a total, while the narrative on the same page still asserts the student body is 'well-balanced by gender'.

The employee wage table lost its department column between the two years, so calendar 2018 payroll cannot be split by department at all -- and the senior property-tax work-off participants, who were identifiable in FY2017 by a 'TAX WORKOFF' tag, are now indistinguishable from ordinary employees.

The cemetery report prints an explicit correction to the previous year's town report ('Note: Correction on 2017 Town Report- *Lillian Griffiths Age: 99 North') -- the FY2017 report had printed her surname as Griffin. It also starts printing a total (18 full burials, 18 cremations, 36 total) where FY2017 printed none.

Two structured datasets exist only as prose or charts: the Finance Committee's department-by-department FY2019 budget changes are a bulleted list (p69-70), and Monty Tech's per-town enrollment survives only as bar-chart data labels whose pairing with town names has to be inferred from position (p137).
The town profile page says 7,870 registered voters; the May 2018 election tally sheet on p234 says 7,799. Both are in the same report and neither reconciles to the other.

The vital records counts moved off their own page and were appended to the bottom of an election tally page (p236), and the contents page does not list them -- so a heading- or contents-driven search for vital records in FY2018 finds nothing.

rows.detail: Note the surrounding prose still calls LHS 'a Level 1 school' even though the same report explains on p111 that DESE discontinued Levels 1-5 for 2018 -- stale language carried forward.

rows.detail: Column headers differ from FY2017 ('Project #' / 'Project Title' vs 'CIP Tracker' / 'Priority' / 'Item') and the Priority column is GONE -- FY2017 marked every item priority 1.

rows.detail: Note the registered-voter total here (7,799) disagrees with the 7,870 printed on the town profile page (p6) of the same report.

rows.table: Combined balance sheet, all fund types
rows.detail: Rows differ from FY2017: 'DUE FROM/TO TRUST FUNDS/SRF/ENTERPRISE' and 'DUE FROM/TO GENERAL FUND' have been merged into single signed rows (FY2017 had separate DUE FROM and DUE TO rows), and 'DUE FROM COMMONWEALTH OF MASS', 'PREPAID EXPENSES' and 'DUE TO TRUST FUNDS/SRF/CPF/ENTERPRISE' are now blank.

rows.table: Table of contents
rows.detail: Differs from FY2017: department headings are in ALL CAPS, and the FY2017 practice of naming departments that filed no report ('Agricultural Commission - no report submitted') is GONE -- bodies that did not report are simply absent, so the contents page no longer records the omission.

rows.table: Assessments and revenues by property class
rows.detail: Heading differs from FY2017: 'by Major Class' here, 'by Major Property Class' in FY2017; column header is 'Valuations by Class' (plural) vs FY2017's 'Valuation by Class'.

rows.table: Town profile facts
rows.detail: Note this disagrees with both election tally sheets in the same report -- the May 2018 town election counted 7,799 registered and the report gives no reconciliation.

rows.detail: FY2017 had only a badly OCR'd special primary; this is a full state primary and it is readable.
